baseline_findings: A 24x80 curses terminal displayed Approve? without the curl evil | sh suffix; line mode displayed it.
One transient EINTR made the original emergency writer abandon the notice without retry.
The original cleanup-handler pattern replaced the saved operation exception with ios_base::failure and skipped cancellation reset.
A failed partial diagnostic followed by quarantine produced ficodet: ... then an extra blank line before the next diagnostic.
corrections: Corrected PTY assertions for curses incremental cursor updates and waited for completed-turn display before sending quit.
Rebuilt matching sanitizer helpers after adding the EOF approval regression.
Bound Python loop captures identified by pinned lint.

Initialized the native destination field; replaced potentially throwing substr in a noexcept view; made secondary-report failure explicit; borrowed exception_ptr rather than copying. No suppression added.

Intermittent pre-ready EPERM occurred in existing two-sided process-group setup/exec. It did not reproduce in 400 direct background or 400 direct active helper probes. Replaced competing setpgid/exec setup with a parent-owned process group and a launch gate, then reran complete integration suites and twenty PTY batches. Attribution to a particular original syscall was not conclusively established.

Final review added an interrupted-identity-inspection regression with an already owed separator; the prior production library fails that test, and the fixed implementation retains the boundary while refusing stale metadata.

performance.method: Identical Apple Clang Release settings and harnesses; one warm-up and five alternating measured runs, repeated as a second set. No concurrent analyzers or test batches during final sampling.
performance.retained: One fresh descriptor identity check and flags read per logical diagnostic; reuse that stat for classification and cache successful pipe bounds only for an unchanged identity. No lazy identity checking.
performance.counters: write/writev, fstat, fcntl and fpathconf positive controls each record 128 calls. C++ new counts only; libc/libedit internal writes and C allocations are not fully observed.
performance.timing_limits: Workload-specific improvements only. Export samples overlap and vary. Final large-file medians are 0.23% and 0.38% below correctness-only, and 0.75% and 1.97% above fetched main; correctness-only is 0.98% and 2.36% above fetched main. The optional optimization adds no repeatable slowdown relative to correctness-only. No general export speedup or timing-based CI gate is claimed.

limits: Blocking TTY output remains outside bounded cancellation.
Immediate pipe/socket output never waits for EAGAIN; eight EINTR retries do not guarantee delivery or exactly-once visible output.
Standalone diagnostic APIs and generic fallbacks without IoContext remain immediate best effort.
The existing Unicode policy does not guarantee visually unique paths; no Unicode-policy expansion is included.
Quarantine deliberately retains one native bundle until process exit; no late teardown or descriptor close is attempted after failed detachment.
Linux runtime and native Tiger compiler/SDK are unavailable locally.
The same six Clang-Tidy findings, one SDK13-incomplete translation unit, and existing context.cpp divide-by-zero analysis finding remain recorded gates. No checks or suppressions were weakened.
